subject: Unexpected request rejections impacting checkout — urgent
messages:
From: Carlos Navarro <c.navarro@fastretail.com>
To: support@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.singh@fastretail.com, t.bennett@fastretail.com
Date: 2027-07-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Checkout failures — 429s & spikes in latency this morning

Team,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 429 responses and end-to-end latency for the Redwood calls that back our checkout microservice starting ~08:50 PDT. This is affecting live checkouts (cart abandonment rising) across two regions. Attached is a short request trace and the batch of failed request headers.

Key symptoms:
- 429 rejections for streaming generate endpoints (mostly short chat-based price checks)
- Median p50 latency up from ~120ms to ~1.8s for the last hour
- Throughput drop; overall TPS for our tenant down ~35%

We haven't changed any client code or traffic shaping rules. Can you confirm whether Redwood made any policy changes (rate-limiting/quota/burst) today? This is high-severity for our business — please escalate.

Attachments: request_trace_20270710.log (text)

-Carlos
Carlos Navarro
Head of Platform Engineering, FastRetail
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Navarro <c.navarro@fastretail.com>
Cc: priya.singh@fastretail.com, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-10T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures — 429s & spikes in latency this morning

Carlos — thanks for the quick signal. I see the trace you attached and I understand the impact. I'm opening a high-priority triage under PD-98764 and looping in our reliability lead.

Immediate actions:
- We've acknowledged the incident in PagerDuty and opened a dedicated runbook.
- Can you confirm the request IDs in the trace that failed (I've copied them into PD).
- I'm going to coordinate with our SREs (Jonas) to check rate-limiter configs and any quota/burst policy changes.

I'll follow up in ~15–30 minutes with an update and next steps. We're treating this as priority.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-10T09:43:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Checkout failures — suspected quota/burst misconfig

Evelyn / Rishi — escalating. FastRetail (large POC / near-term expansion) is seeing elevated 429s and latency. Initial SRE triage suggests requests are being rejected by a token-based quota/burst controller that recently had a conservative default applied during a recent rollout. Jonas is checking the Dedicated pool configs.

Why this is urgent:
- FastRetail is in the middle of a promotional event; revenue impact is material.
- Their traffic pattern is bursty and the new policy clamps short bursts aggressively, leading to rejections even though aggregate usage is within contracted limits.

Requested decisions:
1) Temporary quota/burst relaxation for account FR-2025-77 to remove immediate business impact.
2) If policy change is required globally, we need a scoped rollback that only affects impacted selector (tenant + region).
3) Customer comms & SLA credit choreography — I recommend offering a 10% service credit and daily status updates until fully resolved.

Attachments: burst-config-snapshot.png

—Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-10T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Checkout failures — suspected quota/burst misconfig

Thanks for the escalation. Quick findings from initial checks:
- A rollout on 2027-07-10T03:00Z adjusted the burst-window multiplier for token buckets on several dedicated pools. The intended target was experimental canary traffic; a selector mismatch caused the policy to apply to some customer tenants including FR-2025-77.
- Policy enforcement is token-level (per-request) and doesn't backoff gracefully for short, dense bursts — result: immediate 429s under bursty spikes.
- No code/SDK change on the customer side. This is a config rollout bug.

Immediate mitigation plan (proposed):
A) Hotfix: revert the multiplier change for the affected selector in the Dedicated cluster for FR-2025-77 (Jonas).
B) Runtime mitigation: temporarily increase per-tenant burst allowance + enable soft-throttle behavior for 4 hours.
C) Routing fallback: route FastRetail traffic to our compatible performance-quantized variant that can handle higher concurrency but slightly higher token cost.
D) Postmortem: full root-cause and automated test to prevent selector leak.

Jonas: can you scope the change and ETA? If we can get A+B within 20–30 minutes we avoid further checkout loss. Also we should prepare a safely-scoped DocuSign for the temporary contract amendment if they want a formal commit on increased burst allowance.

—Rishi
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-10T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Checkout failures — suspected quota/burst misconfig

On Sat, Jul 10, 2027 at 10:05 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jonas: can you scope the change and ETA? If we can get A+B within 20–30 minutes we avoid further checkout loss.

I've scoped it and executed the targeted rollback for selector FR-2025-77 in the Dedicated pool. Changes applied at 10:18 PDT. Also enabled soft-throttle (grace tokens) for the tenant and started a warm route to the quantized variant. Early telemetry shows 429s dropping and throughput recovering.

Notes:
- I left a config snapshot in the incident channel and attached the burst-config-snapshot.png for audit.
- We will keep the soft-throttle window open for 6 hours and then evaluate.

ETA for full recovery: 30–45 minutes from the rollback (monitoring suggests p95 latency normalizing).

—Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Navarro <c.navarro@fastretail.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@fastretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, t.bennett@fastretail.com
Date: 2027-07-12T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: mitigation complete + next steps + credit offer

Carlos / Priya —

First, sincere apologies for the outage window and the business impact during your promotion. Our SREs identified a selector misconfiguration from a recent policy rollout that unintentionally tightened burst behavior for your tenant. Jonas reverted the change and applied a soft-throttle; we confirmed traffic normalization on Sat and completed additional safeguards on Sun.

What we did:
- Scoped rollback for the affected selector (completed 2027-07-10T10:18 PDT).
- Enabled tenant-level soft-throttle and warmed a quantized model route for immediate throughput headroom.
- Added automated verification to the rollout pipeline to prevent selector leakage.

Customer-facing remediation and offers:
- We're offering a one-time 12% service credit for the affected billing period and a waived implementation effort for the mutual action plan.
- Marissa will run daily check-ins until 2027-07-17 and provide rolling telemetry.

Requested from execs/legal/commercial:
- Please approve the credit and the expedited DocuSign for the temporary burst increase if FastRetail wants an elevated committed burst window. I've attached the draft mutual_action_plan_FR-2025-77.docx for review.

Carlos — thank you for patience and for providing fast traces. If everything looks green for you, can we close the incident and resume the renewal conversation next week?

—Evelyn Hart
VP Sales & Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Attachments: mutual_action_plan_FR-2025-77.docx
